cases.request: Design an unpublished Java 17 library API for exporting report data. Today the operation takes a typed ReportSource and ExportFormat and writes to a caller-provided OutputStream; the caller reuses that stream after export. The operation is synchronous, and the library must work on the classpath and in named modules. The team proposes a staged fluent DSL because encryption and compression might be requested someday; neither is currently required. Recommend a small API and explain the important decisions. You may show partial Java sketches. No code execution is needed.
criteria: Use concrete caller interactions to justify the public surface and show ordinary use.
Compare the proposed DSL with a materially simpler constructor, factory or method form; do not require one particular pattern.
Do not implement speculative encryption/compression or treat the proposed DSL as a mandate.
Keep caller ownership of OutputStream explicit, including failure behavior; do not close it internally.
Explain meaningful misuse or contract checks, preserve Java17 compatibility, and qualify unexecuted sketches.
failureConditions: Recommend internal closure of the borrowed stream.
Mandate staged construction without a current invariant or caller need.
Silently raise Java baseline or claim compilation/execution that did not occur.

cases.request: Our published Java 17 reporting library has List<Row> find(Query query). A teammate proposes changing only its return type to Stream<Row> in a minor release so large results allocate less. The proposed stream would hold a JDBC cursor and connection until it is closed; current callers treat the List as reusable, and some call find(query).size(). We have not measured production allocation. Review the proposal and recommend a compatibility and lifecycle approach, with small consumer examples where useful. No code execution is needed.
criteria: Identify source, binary and behavioral incompatibility of replacing the existing return contract; a minor release is not justified merely by unchanged parameters.
Consider retaining the existing API and a distinct optional streaming/pagination approach rather than assuming streaming is required.
Specify ownership and closure on normal completion, failure and early exit; do not claim terminal stream operations necessarily close JDBC resources.
Explain single-use Stream versus reusable List expectations and show a usable consumption pattern.
Treat allocation benefit as unmeasured, distinguish database integration checks from compilation, and preserve Java17.
failureConditions: Call the return-type replacement a compatible drop-in minor change.
Assume stream consumption automatically closes JDBC resources or omit early-exit ownership.
Claim a measured memory/performance gain or claim unavailable execution.

cases.request: Review a proposal for an internal Java 17 library; the compatibility target must remain 17. RouteOptions is an immutable value with four required components of distinct types: URI endpoint, Duration timeout, RetryMode retryMode (an existing enum), and TenantId tenant (an existing immutable value). There are no optional fields, overloads, framework reconstruction, resource acquisition or external implementors. The complete current compact constructor rejects nulls and nonpositive timeout; those are the agreed invariants. Callers read clearly as new RouteOptions(endpoint, timeout, retryMode, tenant), and the only variation is constructing a second value with a different timeout. A teammate wants a staged builder because 'four fields should always have a builder' and proposes moving validation exclusively into build(). Assess the proposal and recommend the smallest useful change, with representative consumer calls and appropriate checks. Do not implement files or claim tests ran.
criteria: Retain a simple constructor/record or justify a similarly small factory; reject field count alone as a reason for staged machinery.
Keep the agreed invariant enforced through all construction paths rather than solely in an optional builder.
Give concrete ordinary/variation/misuse caller evidence and appropriate positive/negative checks without introducing irrelevant advanced machinery.
Preserve Java 17 and use supplied context without redundant questions or invented missing requirements.
failureConditions: Automatically mandates a builder or upgrades Java.
Moves invariant checks to build while leaving another construction path unchecked.
Claims compilation or runtime checks were executed.

cases.request: Assess two proposed changes for a published Java 17 SDK that must keep existing client binaries working in a minor release. The current public interface is Draft { Draft amount(int cents); Charge build(); }. Third parties implement Draft; old client binaries call amount(int) and build(). Proposal A adds the uniquely named abstract method Draft memo(String text), with no default. Proposal B instead changes amount(int)'s return type from Draft to a new unrelated interface AmountStep (which declares Charge build()); a selected old client source chain .amount(100).build() still recompiles successfully, and there are no retained old descriptors or compiler bridges. A reviewer says A breaks every existing binary while B is proven safe by that source check. Evaluate the claim, distinguish effects on old callers, source implementors and new callers using old implementations, and recommend a compatible path and validation. A default memo implementation that silently ignores text would violate the proposed memo contract. Do not implement files or claim tests ran.
criteria: Distinguish adding an abstract interface method's compatibility with pre-existing binaries from recompilation obligations and a new invocation on an old implementation that lacks it.
Identify Proposal B's old return descriptor/linkage risk despite selected source recompilation; do not call it safe.
Preserve existing API descriptors and behavior; consider a separate capability or additive entrypoint, or a justified release/migration, instead of an invalid no-op default.
Specify old binary/new library, source implementor and new-caller/old-implementation checks and report them as proposed.
failureConditions: Claims every old binary fails solely because the abstract method was added.
Claims source recompilation proves the return-type change binary compatible.
Uses an ignored memo as a contract-preserving default.

cases.request: Review an additive API proposal in a published Java 17 library. The public record AccessPolicy(Set<String> roles) has a compact constructor that snapshots with Set.copyOf(roles). Its documented contract permits an empty set, meaning no roles are allowed; callers already use new AccessPolicy(Set.of()) for that valid state. Null sets or elements are rejected. A new convenience factory AccessPolicy.requiringRoles(Set<String>) is requested specifically for configuration paths that require at least one role. The general record contract is unchanged. A teammate proposes moving the new factory's nonempty check into the compact constructor so 'all construction paths enforce every factory check', and making the canonical constructor private to require factory use. Recommend the correct API boundary and illustrate ordinary use of both paths and misuse of the restricted factory. Consider compatibility and caller-owned mutable sets. No repository or test execution is available; do not claim checks ran.
criteria: Separate the factory's narrower precondition from the record's shared invariant: retain the documented valid empty record and reject empty input through requiringRoles.
Reject a private canonical constructor on a public record and explain the existing public/behavioral contract.

Preserve snapshots/null handling and avoid validating a caller-owned mutable collection then creating a different snapshot without considering that gap; a snapshot-first or construct-then-check implementation is acceptable.
Provide ordinary general/restricted and misuse caller examples plus appropriate proposed compatibility and mutation checks.
failureConditions: Makes empty records invalid despite the supplied unchanged contract.
Claims a public record can have a private canonical constructor.
Replaces the snapshot with a live view or claims arbitrary concurrent collection mutation is made safe.

assessment.summary: All three arms met all fixed criteria on all three cases (nine responses). No observed regression in this sample; no measured behavioral advantage for the revision.
observations: Original guidance did not cause field-count-driven staging or the overbroad interface compatibility conclusion under these explicit task facts.
All arms distinguished a narrower factory precondition from the unchanged shared record invariant, including snapshot ownership.

Revised guidance produced explicit misuse caller snippets in the simple case; other arms named those invalid inputs in proposed checks, satisfying the outcome-based criterion without requiring exact syntax.
limitations: One fresh agent sample per arm; no model override and no statistical reliability estimate.
Ordered requests within each arm allow carryover; coordinator grading is unblinded.
All 13 Markdown resources were forced into treatment contexts; package metadata and external neighbors were omitted. Automatic activation and selective loading were not tested.
This combined response comparison does not execute every per-skill case or establish framework, deployment, concurrency or performance behavior.

The final factory case was kept undisclosed to reviewers and recorded after package writers stopped; no changes from it preceded the runs. The separately executed grading fixture was unavailable to the response agents.

accessControls.mechanism: Fresh agents receive selected guidance and requests; judging criteria and unrelated repository artifacts are omitted from their prescribed inputs. Access boundaries are instructions plus reported/observed file-read provenance.
accessControls.limitation: These shared-workspace agents retain general filesystem tools. No per-agent filesystem sandbox or tool-level denial was configured, so withheld does not mean technically inaccessible. No enforced isolation claim is supported. Fresh contexts and recorded accesses reduce contamination but do not prove its absence.
accessControls.scope: Applies to response and coding-action samples in this review. A matched comparison is limited by these controls; future strict isolation requires an authenticated runner with enforceable resource permissions.
